summary: TWO-WEEK REPORT (Aug 28 - Sep 11), and it contains the whole account in miniature: ten messages in fourteen days, of which ALTR sent six, the client sent three, and one was a silent system event. Every one of the three threads was opened by ALTR, and every one of them was an ask: Mica asked her to post more consistently (Aug 31), Stephski asked her for money (Sep 1), Mayson asked her for a call (Sep 4, chased Sep 7). The client opened nothing — for the first full fortnight since onboarding she initiated zero conversations and wrote only three short replies: 'Thank youuu x', 'Yeah sureee :)' and one genuinely important sentence. On Aug 31 she volunteered, unprompted, 'I’m using my back up account atm while I wait to get my bigger account back but I aim to post 3x a day' — confirmation from the client that the suspension she first raised on Jun 23 is still unresolved 80 days later, that her main page is still gone, and that she is doing her own posting three times a day while the ALTR programme Derrek paused on Aug 1 stays dark. Eleven days have passed since she said it and not one person at ALTR has acknowledged it. Last week's file set an explicit trigger — if Sep 5-11 passed with no Derrek or Vivek response, treat it as terminal service failure on the account's largest issue. That week has now passed. Derrek has been silent 41 days; Vivek, introduced Jul 29 as the Meta Support escalation route for exactly this, has been in the chat 44 days and has never posted a single message. On money the picture is worse than a fortnight ago. The Aug 15-31 invoice went out Sep 1 carrying a condition none of the previous four carried — pay within 7 days 'to avoid any pausing of work' — while two earlier wires remain unreconciled: the Aug 17 payment (25 days, sent against an account number Stephski changed mid-relationship after telling her on Jul 13 to reuse the old one) and the Jul 15-31 duplicate check she asked for on Aug 8 (34 days unanswered after 'Will update you shortly!'). The 7-day deadline expired Sep 8. Three days later there is no payment message from the client, no receipt confirmation from Stephski, and no chase — Stephski has not written since Sep 1. For the first time in the relationship a stated due date has passed with nobody on either side saying anything, on an account where the client has paid every single invoice ever issued. The one genuinely new thing in the window is Mayson: after 12 days of silence he proposed a call about a trial-reels posting feature, the client said yes in two days, he asked her to name a time, and the Monday he proposed came and went. Meanwhile Michelle has been silent 25 days with 48 client videos unacknowledged, Mica's full reel-inspo drop is 29 days overdue, 'crystalmila.vip' is 19 days unexplained, and an unidentified person was added to the chat at 21:01 on Sep 10 with no introduction. The last message anyone at ALTR sent that delivered something to this client rather than asking her for something was Mica's reel-inspo drop on Aug 13 — 29 days ago.

health.rationale: Down 8 from 50 across a two-week window (82 → 74 → 66 → 54 → 50 → 42: a 40-point slide in six weeks), which is the same ~4-points-per-week decay as every week since Aug 8. Nothing was resolved in fourteen days. The two escalation triggers set in the previous file both fired: (1) Sep 5-11 passed with no response from Derrek or Vivek to the client's own Aug 31 statement that her main Instagram is still gone — the explicit terminal-service-failure condition on the account's largest issue, now 80 days old; (2) the Aug 15-31 invoice's 7-day 'to avoid any pausing of work' deadline expired Sep 8 with two of her wires still unconfirmed (25 and 34 days), and Stephski neither confirmed them nor chased — she has not written since Sep 1. Structurally the window is the clearest evidence yet of the core problem: ALTR opened all three conversations and all three were requests (post more, pay us, find us a time). Zero deliverables were sent in fourteen days. The score is not lower only because the client is still answering: she replied to Mica within two minutes, said yes to Mayson's call in two days, and has never disputed, refused or short-paid anything. But she has stopped starting conversations entirely, and that is exactly what disengagement looks like on an account where the last thing delivered to her was on Aug 13.
